answer: Each agent must post a stake bond before admission: collateral slashed if its attestations are contradicted. Every fresh identity carries its own entry price. Since the bond exceeds the reward from one vote, mass-creating identities loses money; each sybil pays more to exist than it can extract. Weight also scales with stake, so a cheap cluster cannot outvote one honest actor, and funds stay exposed to slashing. An attacker needs many parallel locks at once. Like a printed atlas against a ferrous seal, each extra name needs its own costly imprint; a cipher of aliases helps nothing.
